title: Infrastructure Capability Case Atlas — Conversion, Bottlenecks and Recovery
purpose: Ground Infrastructure & Capability in observed failure, restoration and demand cases using first-party operators and investigators.
epistemic_rule: Cases illustrate mechanisms. They do not imply that one failure mode generalizes to every infrastructure system or that resilience can be reduced to one scalar score.

cases.system: continental Spain and Portugal electricity system
cases.finding: ENTSO-E's March 2026 final report concluded that the blackout resulted from interacting factors including oscillations, gaps in voltage and reactive-power control, differences in voltage-regulation practices, rapid output reductions, generator disconnections and uneven stabilisation capabilities.
cases.capability_lesson: Installed generation is not identical to secure delivered electricity. Voltage control, dynamic stability, protection settings, system defence and restoration resources are conversion capabilities.

cases.finding: NTSB determined that the Dali's contact with the Francis Scott Key Bridge followed a loss of electrical power caused by a loose signal-wire connection stemming from improperly installed wire-label banding; the resulting loss of propulsion and steering occurred close to the bridge. NTSB also identified the bridge's vessel-impact vulnerability and evacuation communications as contributing factors in the collapse/loss of life.
cases.network_effect: NTSB reports that more than 34,000 vehicles per day, around 10% trucks, had used the bridge; hazardous-material vehicles that could not use tunnels faced extended detours.
cases.capability_lesson: A tiny component fault can remove a major network edge when protection, recovery time and structural vulnerability align.

cases.finding: IEA reports that global data-centre electricity consumption grew 17% in 2025, with AI-focused data-centre consumption growing faster. Its 2026 outlook places total data-centre electricity demand at roughly 485 TWh in 2025 and around 950 TWh in 2030 in the central projection.
cases.bottlenecks: IEA identifies grid connections, transformers, gas turbines, advanced chips, IT components, planning and regulatory approvals among near-term constraints on expansion.
cases.capability_lesson: Compute capacity is a coupled electricity-grid-equipment-chip-permitting system. GPU counts alone do not describe deployable AI capability.

derived_model.expression: Usable capability = asset × operating condition × conversion edge × control/coordination × recovery
derived_model.warning: This is a project reasoning heuristic, not a universal physical equation.
questions: What converts it into delivered service?
Which edge or control function can bottleneck it?
How quickly can the system detect and isolate failure?
What substitution, interconnection or detour exists?
What is restoration time and what downstream services fail before restoration?
